findings.message: The same `_sc_rc_file` is passed to both the batch call (line 253) and each individual per-spec fallback call (line 273); the last `printf '%s' "$?"` written by any call overwrites earlier writes, so if the batch times out (rc=124) but one subsequent individual fallback call succeeds (rc=0), `_sc_router_rc` is read as 0 and `_sc_disposition` is reported as 'complete' — masking the batch timeout and preventing `_route_escalate_timeout` from growing the budget on the next retry cycle; the test covers only the all-calls-fail scenario.

When `mktemp` fails and `_scv_rc_file` is empty, the inner subshell executes `printf '%s' "$?" > ""` which generates a bash error on stderr (suppressed by `|| true`) but silently abandons the rc capture, causing `_rtm_rc` to remain 0 and the disposition to stay 'complete' even when `route_to_model` times out; `spec-correspondence` avoids this with the safer `${_rc_file:-/dev/null}` pattern but `spec-coverage` does not apply the same guard.
